Olhopil New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Olhopil, established in the 17th century under the name Roguzka, saw its Jewish community reach 2,473 people (30 percent) by 1897, owning a brewery, wood stores, one of the town's two printing houses, and every inn, watchmaker's shop, teahouse, and photo shop. The community endured two pogroms in 1919 alone, in May and again on Yom Kippur that October. Following the 1941 occupation, a ghetto here held local Jews and deportees from Bessarabia, with a typhus epidemic claiming many lives that winter; in 1943, an Italian military unit stationed in the town fed the ghetto's Jewish children.
